newsitem.title: USA: Winter wheat sowings plunge, U.S. supply seen tight.
newsitem.headline: Winter wheat sowings plunge, U.S. supply seen tight.

text.p: American farmers sowed only 48.2 million acres of winter wheat, the smallest total since 1978, suggesting a scanty wheat stockpile for at least another year, the Agriculture Department said Friday.

It forecast 374 million bushels of wheat would be on hand -- well below normal -- when the new crop was ready for harvest this summer. Some 1.22 billion bushels were in U.S. grain bins and warehouses on Dec. 1, about what analysts expected, but the smallest figure for that time of the year since 1987.
